newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ariane-5 selected for scientific satellite.
newsitem.headline: Ariane-5 selected for scientific satellite.

text.p: Western Europe's Arianespace company said on Tuesday it had won a contract to launch a scientific satellite for the European Space Agency (ESA) aboard its new generation Ariane-5 rocket.

The company said that the XMM (X-ray Multi-Mirror) satellite designed to help scientists explore the universe and observe the earth would be launched from Kourou in French Guyana in the summer of 1999 or the winter of 1999-2000.
In a statement issued at the Paris airshow, the company said the Ariane-5 heavy-lift launch system was chosen because of the XMM's size, weight and mission characteristics.
The contract brings Arianespace's satellite backlog at 43 satellites to be launched worth an estimated $3.4 billion. Financial terms of this contract were not disclosed.
But the future of the Ariane-5 rocket is in serious doubt. The first Ariane-5 exploded 37 seconds after its maiden launch in June 1996 in a major setback for Europe's 10-year, $9 billion programme.

Arianespace was scheduled to take over commercial operations of Ariane-5 earlier this year, but a second experimental launch, the 502, is slated for late September at the earliest and further delays are likely, officials said.
